every child_process launcher by name: spawn, spawnSync, execFile, execFileSync, exec, execSync, fork
a launcher through a renamed import, a member bound to a variable, a destructured member and a namespace member
a launched binary named by a same-file string constant, and execPath read on process or on a binding of it
an argv array naming a roster binary first (gp, bd, furnace, kill, pkill, killall, sh, bash, zsh, dash, ksh), a shell's -c script followed
a shell command line split into simple commands: NAME=value assignments and an env prefix skipped, ; & | and newlines split, quotes removed
a shell's -c script in a launcher's argv, a -c flag cluster, a templated script's static head and a script nested in a script
a templated shell line's static head, and a launcher's whitespace-bearing command (shell: true)
process.kill read on process, globalThis.process, globalThis['process'], by element access and through a type assertion
kill named by an import from the process module (renamed included) or destructured from process or a require of it
kill on a binding of the process object: a default, namespace or import-equals import, a require, a variable alias (chains followed to a fixpoint, in any order)
stop on every Furnace stop owner: runs, attempts, supervision, host
stop by element access, on an owner by element access, through an owner bound to a variable or destructured, and stop destructured from an owner
stop on a Run or Attempt handle by name (run, runX, attempt, attemptX, xRun, xAttempt) or bound to a variable
every bd read verb reads when it carries no writing flag: show, list, ready, blocked, search, stats, status, count, info, where, version, help, graph, doctor
a bd launch writes when its verb is not a read verb, or is not a literal
every Agent SDK session function by named and renamed import, and a session function read on a namespace import
a workflow host launched as a Worker, bare or as a namespace member
the gp binary as a string token: bare gp, an absolute path, gp.exe and gp.cmd
gp launched through the GraphPolicyCLI package: npx graph-policy-cli and node with the package's entry
gp wire vocabulary in code tokens: GraphDataIR, a graphpolicy.<surface>.v<n> schema id, GP_RPC_ and GP_CLI_ codes
the GP_CLI_UNKNOWN_COMMAND refusal code named
the train word in a string token, alone or inside a command line
import() and require() of a computed specifier
a GraphPolicyCLI family name in a module specifier and in an identifier

a bd read verb with a writing flag writes (bd 1.1.0-rc.1 help): ready --claim, doctor --fix, doctor --fix-child-parent and doctor --clean, bare or in --flag=value form, anywhere in the argv; a word that only begins with one (--claimed, --fixes, --cleanup) is not one
a bd launch's verb is its first lowercase word, so leading flags are skipped: bd --json show reads, bd -q close writes
a command in a subshell ( ), a $( ) or a backtick command substitution, outside quotes, is a simple command of its own; parentheses inside quotes stay text

a command a shell reserved word opens (!, {, if, then, elif, else, do, while, until) with the word skipped, the closing }, fi, done and esac running nothing, and a reserved word after a command's first word kept as an argument
a command behind the exec builtin, with exec's options skipped: -c, -l and -a with its name

env, bare or by path, with its options before the command: a flag such as -i, - or --ignore-environment, -u, -C, --unset and --chdir with their value or in --option=value form, then NAME=value assignments
a roster binary named with a .exe or .cmd suffix, bare or by path: bd.exe, furnace.cmd, pkill.exe, a shell (bash.exe) whose -c script is followed, and an argv array headed by one
process read through each wrapper the census unwraps beside parentheses and as: satisfies, an angle-bracket assertion and a non-null assertion, on a member read and on a variable initializer
exec, like execSync, runs a templated command line read by its static head
a shell's -c script followed four shells deep: sh runs bash, bash runs zsh, zsh runs dash and dash runs the command
a GraphPolicyCLI family name and gp wire vocabulary in a private class member name (#graphPolicy, #GraphDataIR)
the train word in a template literal's static head, middle and tail
a launcher name imported type-only (import { type spawnSync as run }) binds no launcher, so a call through that name records no launch
